answer: Coordination-Tax Admission Bonds. Each agent pays a small fee per outbound coordination edge, priced by the raven density of its neighborhood, so dense clusters pay more. A pearl of shared entropy seeds each identity, making near-duplicate agents detectable and double-taxed. An idle sparrow account accrues no credit and must prepay full price. Attackers pay rising per-sybil cost plus detection penalties; honest sparse agents pay little.
